title: Kinodynamic exploration and reconstruction
description: Exploration planners evaluate informative trajectory segments that respect UAV dynamics and maintain useful motion.
introduction: An informative viewpoint is useful only if a UAV can reach it efficiently. KRH-NBVP considers feasible motion while choosing where to observe next, and KAEP adds a global planning component to reach informative regions that remain beyond a local search.

problem.heading: Choose a motion, as well as a view.
paragraphs: A planner that selects viewpoints geometrically can ask a UAV to make sharp turns or repeatedly slow down. Reaching each observation point then consumes time that a viewpoint-only score may not represent.

Local exploration can also reach a point where nearby candidates reveal little new space. Efficient reconstruction needs both dynamically feasible motion and a way to reach informative regions elsewhere in the map.

approach.heading: Build the vehicle’s dynamics into exploration.
paragraphs: KRH-NBVP builds a tree of feasible trajectory segments that respect the UAV’s speed and acceleration limits. Candidate trajectories are evaluated using information gain, trajectory length and how well they maintain speed.
KAEP combines this local kinodynamic exploration with a global planning component. It can direct the vehicle towards remaining informative regions when local progress becomes limited.

A separate 2026 contribution studies centralized multi-UAV exploration and reconstruction using existing single-UAV planners. That framework is a related extension; the outdoor camera and reconstruction footage shown here belongs to the single-UAV kinodynamic evaluation.

steps.title: Generate feasible segments
steps.text: Build candidate trajectories that respect speed and acceleration limits.

steps.title: Score information and motion
steps.text: Consider new space, distance travelled and maintained speed together.

steps.title: Replan from new observations
steps.text: Update the map as the UAV executes its selected motion.

steps.title: Reach remaining regions
steps.text: Use KAEP’s global component when local exploration becomes less informative.

evidence.label: Simulation comparison
evidence.text: Simulation evaluates the effect of selecting kinodynamically feasible trajectory segments rather than geometric next-best viewpoints. The KRH-NBVP clip illustrates this planning behaviour.

evidence.label: Outdoor onboard mapping and planning
evidence.text: In the lamp-structure experiment at Instituto Superior Técnico, a UAV uses an RGB-D camera while mapping and trajectory planning run onboard. The supplied real-flight evaluation uses RTK-GPS/IMU localization.

evidence.label: Three-trial real-flight comparison
evidence.text: Mean time to 95% coverage over three real trials per planner was 36.77 s for KAEP, 47.95 s for KRH-NBVP, 50.68 s for AEP and 89.27 s for RH-NBVP. These values refer to the same source evaluation and completion criterion.

evidence.label: Related centralized multi-UAV framework
evidence.text: The ICARM 2026 paper is listed separately from the RA-L kinodynamic article. Its multi-UAV framework should not inherit the single-UAV hardware timings above.
